blocks.text: Setting up your Google Sheets workspace on Mac

Google Sheets is a web app. It does not have a native Mac installer. You can still make it feel like a desktop app. Open Chrome and go to sheets.google.com. Click the three dots at the top right of the browser window. Select Cast, Save, and Share. Click Install page as app. This adds a shortcut to your Launchpad and Dock. You can now open your sales trackers in a separate window.

Speed matters when you are logging dozens of leads. Your hands should stay on the keyboard. Press ⌘ + / to open the full list of shortcuts. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to open the find and replace menu. If you need to hide a row, select it and press ⌘ + ⌥ + 9. Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 0 to hide columns. These small movements save hours over a month.

SDRs often deal with messy data. You might have duplicates from different lead sources. Use the built-in tools to clean your list. Highlight your data range. Go to Data > Data cleanup > Remove duplicates. This keeps your outreach focused on unique prospects. You can also split names into first and last columns using Data > Split text to columns.

Lazur lives in your Mac notch. It sees your screen and hears your voice. When you are stuck in a complex sheet, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask for help. Lazur points at the menu you need. It explains how to build a formula. It can even help you find where you saved a specific prospect file.

items: Keeping too many tabs open. Use a tab manager to group your CRM and Sheets.
Ignoring the cell limit. If your sheet hits 20 million cells, it will lag.
Manual data entry errors. Use dropdown menus to standardize your lead status.
Forgetting to share with view-only access. Always check your link settings before sending to your manager.

blocks.text: How to stay organized as an SDR

You spend about 10 percent of your week switching tools. Try to keep your research and tracking in one place. Use Google Sheets for your daily outreach list. Keep your CRM for final logging. This separation prevents browser sprawl. If you get overwhelmed, ask Lazur to dictate a quick note about your next task.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No. Google Sheets is a web application. You can create a desktop shortcut using Chrome to make it open in its own window.

faq.question: How many cells can I have in one Google Sheet?
faq.answer: As of September 2026, the limit is 20 million cells per spreadsheet.

faq.question: How do I see all keyboard shortcuts in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ + / while inside any Google Sheet to open the shortcut helper.
